regime: memory-bound (working hypothesis; process synchronization also limits scaling)
ideal_dram_traffic_assumption: Perfect spatial/row reuse: input loaded once (8 B/cell), output written once (8 B/cell), write-allocate overhead excluded; finite-grid boundary terms ignored.
ufunc_traffic_note: First add 24 B, next three adds 24 B each, final in-place multiply16 B. These are logical load/store bytes, not measured DRAM traffic; chunk cache reuse reduces DRAM traffic.

copy_bandwidth_probe.method: single-process NumPy copyto of 128 MiB float64 array
copy_bandwidth_probe.caveat: Logical read+write bytes; no hardware DRAM counter; write allocation and cache effects are not measured.

cache_profile.cache_notes: Generic hw.l1/l2 describe a reported cache domain; heterogeneous per-level sizes are authoritative. Unreported L3 is null, not zero.

classification_evidence: Low arithmetic intensity and a memory-streaming five-point stencil make bandwidth/cache traffic a plausible bottleneck. The NumPy implementation also performs multiple ufunc passes. Observed process barriers and scheduler overhead can dominate; no hardware counters establish actual DRAM saturation.
classification_limit: A complete measured Roofline needs DRAM bytes and a calibrated compute roof. Those are unavailable here; memory-bound is a model-based hypothesis, not a hardware-counter finding. Copy bandwidth is observed and not a theoretical peak.

amdahl_fit.model: T(P)/T(1) = s + (1-s)/P; least squares on normalized runtimes
amdahl_fit.fit_constraint: s restricted to [0,1]; unconstrained value retained
amdahl_fit.ceiling_note: null means infinite in the fitted ideal model; extrapolation is not a measured hardware guarantee
amdahl_fit.limitations: Memory contention, process barriers and heterogeneous cores violate a constant serial-fraction model.

strong.source: median of this strong mode's own P=1 raw compute times

weak.source: median of this weak mode's own P=1 raw compute times

gustafson_model_note: Illustrative P-s*(P-1) curve using the serial fraction fitted to strong-scaling runtimes. This reuses a strong-scaling model parameter; it does not measure the serial time fraction of each scaled weak workload and is not an empirical Gustafson-Barsis verification. Observed weak throughput is reported separately.
